critique.evidence: Strong cyber-editorial identity, restrained cyan/red palette, clear headline hierarchy, and a convincing desktop composition. However, tablet and especially mobile become excessively tall and dense; the red artifact panel dominates the page, small mono labels and muted copy are difficult to scan, and several mobile lines wrap awkwardly. The global header also feels clipped rather than intentionally responsive: navigation disappears offscreen, the mobile wordmark is absent, and the visible “SWIPE →” cue competes with truncated items. Contrast evidence for header links remains incomplete at tablet and mobile, so polish is not fully proven.
critique.fix: Create a deliberate compact mobile artifact layout, increase small-text size/contrast, reduce vertical padding and forced wrapping, and redesign the header with a persistent compact brand plus an explicit menu or polished scroll treatment. Re-capture with verified header contrast.
